identity.name: TIM IOC Feed Match — TAXII-Fed C2 Indicator + Outbound NDR Session Stitch (T1071.001 / T1568)
identity.summary: XSIAM TIM subscribes to the lab mocktaxii TAXII 2.1 collection, ingesting STIX indicators for the planted fake-C2 IP and five Route53 IOC subdomains. A lab host then beacons to one of them via the c2_http_beacon EAL plugin. The TIM value is the IOC match: TIM flags the destination against its TAXII feed and a correlation rule stitches the feed-match to the NDR session into one C2 incident.
identity.description: Threat Intelligence Management is the plane where externally-sourced indicators become actionable detections. This card validates the full TIM loop against the lab tim IaC topology (infra/modules/aws/tim/): a mocktaxii STIX/TAXII 2.1 server on port 9000 serves a default collection whose indicators name the fake-C2 IP and five Route53 private-zone subdomains under <project>-tim.internal — c2-beacon, exfil-drop, payload-delivery, dga-1a2b3c, and cryptominer-pool — every one of which resolves to the fake-C2 HTTP endpoint on port 8000. XSIAM TIM subscribes to that collection, so the indicators land in the threat_intel feed and the IOC objects are armed. The detection surface has two halves that only TIM can fuse. First, the TIM half: when any endpoint or NGFW session touches one of the feed-listed domains or the C2 IP, XSIAM raises an IOC match — this is the unique TIM value, turning a benign-looking outbound HTTP session into a known-bad verdict purely from the subscribed feed. Second, the NDR half: the NGFW Enhanced Application Log / network_story records the outbound session (DNS resolution of the IOC subdomain, then the HTTP GET to the resolved fake-C2 IP). Neither alone is sufficient — NDR sees an allowed web-browsing session to an internal IP, and the raw feed is just a list — but the correlation rule joins the IOC-feed-match to the NDR session on src_host within a tight window, demonstrating that the subscribed TAXII feed actually drove an incident. The matching outbound traffic is generated by the CortexSim c2_http_beacon EAL plugin pointed at the planted IOC subdomain, carrying the X-Simulation-Run-ID operator header so a DC can isolate the simulated sessions during a POV. All targets are inside the deployed VPC (private Route53 zone + in-VPC fake C2) — safe by design, no real malicious infrastructure is contacted.

execution.framework_reference_id: T1071.001 — CortexSim c2_http_beacon EAL plugin pointed at a TAXII-fed IOC subdomain (c2-beacon.<project>-tim.internal) resolving to the in-VPC fake C2

prerequisites.description: Lab matching scenario SIM-TIM-001: the tim IaC module deployed (mocktaxii TAXII 2.1 on :9000, fake C2 on :8000, Route53 private zone with the 5 planted IOC subdomains).
XSIAM TIM connector subscribed to the mocktaxii collection so the C2 IP + IOC domains land in the threat_intel feed.
prerequisites.check_command: echo 'verify threat_intel dataset contains indicator for c2-beacon.<project>-tim.internal'

prerequisites.description: NGFW (or Suricata lab stand-in) forwarding session + DNS logs into XSIAM so network_story / panw_ngfw_traffic_raw is populated for the outbound leg.
prerequisites.check_command: echo 'verify panw_ngfw_traffic_raw is receiving logs in XSIAM'

payload.code:
# All targets are inside the deployed VPC (private Route53 IOC zone + in-VPC fake C2) — safe by design.
TIM_ZONE="${TIM_ZONE:-cortexsim-tim.internal}"
# step-1: confirm the TAXII collection is reachable and serving the planted indicators
curl -sf "http://localhost:9000/taxii2/" -H 'Accept: application/taxii+json;version=2.1' | jq -e '.api_roots | length >= 1'
# step-2: generate the matching outbound traffic against the TAXII-fed IOC subdomain via the EAL plugin
cat > /tmp/tim-ioc-beacon.yml <<YML
campaign_id: CMP-TIM-001
name: "TIM validation — IOC feed match beacon"
authorized_by: "domain-consultant@paloaltonetworks.com"
simulation_authorized: true
target_allowlist:
  - c2-beacon.${TIM_ZONE}
dry_run: false
tags: [tim, ioc-match, c2-beacon, eal]
steps:
  - step_id: step-01
    plugin: c2_http_beacon
    params:
      target_url: http://c2-beacon.${TIM_ZONE}:8000/checkin
      iterations: 12
      sleep_seconds: 30
      jitter_pct: 20
      method: GET
      dga_query_param: true
YML
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/tim-ioc-beacon.yml --live

input_variables.name: TIM_ZONE
input_variables.description: Route53 private-zone suffix from the tim IaC module (terraform output tim_internal_zone), e.g. cortexsim-tim.internal.

expected_artifacts.description: DNS resolution of a TAXII-fed IOC subdomain (c2-beacon.<zone>) to the fake-C2 IP.
Outbound HTTP session from the lab host to the resolved fake-C2 IP on port 8000.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: dst_host contains "c2-beacon." AND dst_port = 8000 AND action = "allow"

expected_artifacts.description: XSIAM TIM IOC match raised for the destination against the subscribed TAXII feed.
Operator header X-Simulation-Run-ID present on every simulated HTTP request for POV filtering.

cleanup.code:
rm -f /tmp/tim-ioc-beacon.yml
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-TIM-001 cleanup complete — no persistent artifacts'

iocs.context: Planted Route53 private-zone subdomain served by the tim IaC module and published by the mocktaxii STIX/TAXII 2.1 collection. Resolves to the in-VPC fake-C2 IP. The canonical TIM value: an outbound session to this name is benign to NDR until the subscribed feed marks it known-bad.
Planted exfiltration IOC subdomain in the mocktaxii feed; resolves to the fake C2. Used to validate that a second feed-listed indicator also fires an IOC match.
DGA-style planted IOC subdomain in the mocktaxii feed (T1568 Dynamic Resolution); resolves to the fake C2. Validates feed-driven detection of algorithmically-named C2 hosts.

biocs.name: TIM — Outbound Session to TAXII-Fed IOC Domain Carrying Simulation Header
biocs.description: NGFW EAL — outbound HTTP to a planted TIM IOC subdomain (.internal C2 zone) carrying the X-Simulation-Run-ID operator header. Behavioral leg that ties the simulated beacon to a feed-listed destination so the DC can isolate POV sessions.
biocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter app in ("web-browsing", "http")
| filter dst_host contains_any ("c2-beacon.", "exfil-drop.", "payload-delivery.", "dga-1a2b3c.", "cryptominer-pool.")
| filter dst_host contains ".internal"
| filter http_req_headers contains "X-Simulation-Run-ID"
| filter action = "allow"
| fields _time, src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host, app, uri, http_user_agent, http_req_headers

xql_queries.name: TIM Pre-flight — TAXII Feed Indicators Ingested Into Threat Intel
xql_queries.query:
dataset = threat_intel
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400)
| filter feed_source = "mocktaxii" or feed_name contains "mocktaxii"
| filter indicator_type = "domain-name" or indicator_type = "ipv4-addr"
| comp count() as indicators by feed_source
| filter indicators >= 1
| fields feed_source, indicators

xql_queries.name: TIM IOC Match — Outbound Session to TAXII-Fed C2 Domain
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter app in ("web-browsing", "http", "dns", "ssl")
| filter dst_host contains_any ("c2-beacon.", "exfil-drop.", "payload-delivery.", "dga-1a2b3c.", "cryptominer-pool.")
| join type=inner (dataset = threat_intel | filter feed_source = "mocktaxii" | filter indicator_type = "domain-name" | fields indicator_value) as feed feed.indicator_value = dst_host
| comp count() as ioc_hits, count_distinct(dst_host) as matched_indicators by src_ip
| filter ioc_hits >= 1
| fields src_ip, matched_indicators, ioc_hits

xql_queries.name: TIM — Periodic Beacon to Feed-Listed IOC Domain (NDR leg)
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter app in ("web-browsing", "http")
| filter dst_host contains "c2-beacon." and dst_host contains ".internal"
| filter action = "allow"
| comp count() as beacon_count, count_distinct(http_user_agent) as ua_variants, avg(bytes_sent) as avg_bytes_sent by src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host
| filter beacon_count >= 8
| fields src_ip, dst_ip, dst_host, beacon_count, ua_variants, avg_bytes_sent

xql_queries.name: TIM Stitch — IOC Feed Match Joined to NDR Session on Source Host
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter dst_host contains ".internal"
| join type=inner (dataset = threat_intel | filter feed_source = "mocktaxii" | filter indicator_type = "domain-name" | fields indicator_value) as feed feed.indicator_value = dst_host
| comp count_distinct(dst_host) as matched_iocs, count() as sessions, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by src_ip
| filter matched_iocs >= 1 and sessions >= 8
| fields src_ip, matched_iocs, sessions, first_seen, last_seen

xql_queries.name: TIM — Any Host Resolving a DGA-Style Feed-Listed Subdomain (T1568)
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400)
| filter app = "dns" or dns_query_name != null
| filter dns_query_name contains "dga-1a2b3c." and dns_query_name contains ".internal"
| comp count() as resolutions by src_ip, dns_query_name
| fields src_ip, dns_query_name, resolutions

correlation_rules.name: TIM — TAXII IOC Feed Match Stitched to Outbound NDR Session
correlation_rules.logic: (XQL(TIM IOC Match — Outbound Session to TAXII-Fed C2 Domain) AND XQL(TIM — Periodic Beacon to Feed-Listed IOC Domain (NDR leg))) -> join on src_host within 60s. Promotes the benign-looking outbound web session to a C2 incident because the destination resolves against the subscribed mocktaxii TAXII feed.

correlation_rules.name: TIM — IOC Feed Match With Operator-Tagged Simulation Session
correlation_rules.logic: BIOC(TIM — Outbound Session to TAXII-Fed IOC Domain Carrying Simulation Header) AND IOC(domain: c2-beacon.cortexsim-tim.internal) -> single incident. Confirms the simulated beacon session is both feed-matched and operator-isolable via X-Simulation-Run-ID.

use_cases.name: Threat Intel Management — TAXII Feed IOC Match + NDR Stitch
use_cases.description: Validate that XSIAM TIM ingests the mocktaxii TAXII 2.1 collection, raises an IOC match when a lab host beacons to a feed-listed C2 domain, and stitches that feed-match to the NGFW outbound session into a single C2 incident.

test_cases.objective: The subscribed mocktaxii TAXII feed is ingested and an IOC match fires on the outbound session to the planted C2 domain.
preconditions: tim IaC module deployed (mocktaxii :9000, fake C2 :8000, Route53 IOC zone).
XSIAM TIM connector subscribed to the mocktaxii collection.
NGFW (or Suricata lab) forwarding session + DNS logs into XSIAM.
steps: Run SIM-TIM-001 step-01 (confirm TAXII collection reachable) and step-02 (ingest-check XQL).
Run SIM-TIM-001 step-03 (live beacon to c2-beacon.<zone>:8000, 12 iterations).
Inspect threat_intel + panw_ngfw_traffic_raw for the source host.
success_criteria: XQL `TIM Pre-flight — TAXII Feed Indicators Ingested Into Threat Intel` returns >= 1 row.
XQL `TIM IOC Match — Outbound Session to TAXII-Fed C2 Domain` returns >= 1 row.
XQL `TIM — Periodic Beacon to Feed-Listed IOC Domain (NDR leg)` returns >= 1 row with beacon_count >= 8.

test_cases.objective: The IOC feed match stitches to the NDR session into a single C2 incident, and the simulated session is operator-isolable.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-TIM-0001` groups the IOC feed match and the NGFW session on src_host into one incident_id.
XQL `TIM Stitch — IOC Feed Match Joined to NDR Session on Source Host` returns >= 1 row.
BIOC `TIM — Outbound Session to TAXII-Fed IOC Domain Carrying Simulation Header` matches every simulated request.

preventive_controls: Subscribe XSIAM TIM to high-fidelity TAXII 2.1 feeds and arm matching against NGFW + endpoint telemetry so feed-listed indicators block at egress.
Enforce URL Filtering + Advanced Threat Prevention on egress policy; deny direct outbound from server subnets to non-sanctioned destinations.
Apply App-ID least-privilege egress rules so only sanctioned applications and destinations leave the network.
detection_engineering: Join TIM IOC-feed matches to the NGFW/endpoint session that touched the indicator on a shared src_host within a tight window rather than alerting on the raw feed match alone.
Score feed provenance (which TAXII collection, indicator age, confidence) into the incident so analysts can triage feed quality.
Hunt for hosts resolving DGA-style feed-listed subdomains (T1568) even when the subsequent session is blocked.
